headline: The US government plans to lend the power company Vistra about $4 billion to upgrade three of its nuclear plants, Bloomberg reports.
score_reason: Lowered from 7: one outlet quoting unnamed sources, and neither the government nor Vistra has confirmed the loan yet.
importance_line: Customers of the power grid that serves about 67 million people and is struggling with data center demand could get more nuclear power sooner than from new reactors, but the loan is unconfirmed and the size of the extra output is not known.
summary: Bloomberg reports, citing unnamed people familiar with the matter, that the Trump administration plans to offer Vistra a loan package of about $4 billion to upgrade three nuclear plants, two in Ohio and one in Pennsylvania. Energy Secretary Chris Wright could announce it as soon as Monday, but neither the Energy Department nor Vistra had immediately responded to requests for comment, and the size of the planned expansions was not yet known.
notes: Bloomberg text read on Yahoo Finance; source and url are Yahoo Finance's, original reporting by Bloomberg.
